text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency SLO breach for /v1/streaming/generate (region=us-west-2). p95=220ms p99=2.3s over the last 5m. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/latency/streaming?from=now-10m
Maya: acked, I'm oncall. pulling up dashboards now :eyes:
Alex: saw the page, noticing a spike in tail latency correlated with increase in streaming stall errors in logs ("stream write timeout"). Any known deploys?
Maya: no deploys in the last 30m per deploy-bot. checking autoscaler and GPU queue lengths
Anna (SRE): I can jump in — tagging @Maya. Initial quick checks: can you curl the health endpoint on a couple of replicas? if streaming endpoint stalls it's probably backpressure on runtime or network egress.
Maya: run quick curl on a sample instance: ``curl -v --no-buffer https://runtime-usw2-12.redwood/api/stream -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'`` returns partial tokens then stalls after ~1.8s
Alex: grabbing metrics: ``rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/streaming/generate"}[5m])`` shows growth in >1s bucket. p99 jump matches request queueing.
Sam (CS): flagging customer impact: a handful of enterprise customers reported degraded streaming UX — some see long pauses mid-streaming, screenshots incoming. No data loss reported.
Kevin (Product): priority: reduce customer visible stalls. What's the lowest-risk mitigation? rollback model variant? reduce max_parallel_streams?
Anna (SRE): low-risk fast mitigations: 1) force-fallback routing to smaller model variant with lower token latency (route: canary->baseline), 2) disable heavy batching for streaming routes, 3) temporarily increase dedicated GPUs if capacity-limited. Which can we do fastest?
Maya: I can toggle batching policy to "off for streaming" via console now. Doing it. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Maya: batching disabled. monitoring...
incident-bot: NOTE: autoscaler activity detected. scale-up event queued for pool gpu-pool-usw2 (requested +2 nodes).
Alex: checking nodes: ``kubectl get pods -n runtime | grep runtime | wc -l`` shows 28 pods, nodes at ~92% GPU util on a subset of pods (from node-exporter). Some pods show high GPU memory and queue depth.
Anna (SRE): can we check KV cache hit rates? if cache thrashing then latency increases.``query: irate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m]) / irate(kv_cache_calls_total[5m])``
Maya: KV cache hit rate steady ~86%. not the main cause. logs show repeated "write timeout after 1200ms" for streaming writers.
Alex: that suggests downstream write stalls — likely client-side or network egress. But we've concurrent increase only for streaming route. Could be a lib change in runtime. Any recent runtime config changes?
Maya: there was a config rollout to change async write buffers three hours ago, flagged as low-risk. I'm rolling that config back now.
Maya: rolling back async-write-buffer-size to previous value via config service. :wrench:
pagerduty-bot: Paging escalation sent to eng-runtime team and infra lead.
Anna (SRE): while rollback proceeds, recommend enabling fallback model routing for high-latency requests: set route policy to prefer model-small when latency >1s. I can apply that policy.
Kevin (Product): do it. want minimal UX regression for customers.
Anna (SRE): applying policy change... done. routing now favors model-small for streaming requests above 1s threshold.
Maya: after disabling batching + rollback + routing change, p99 has dropped to ~700ms in last 2m. p95 ~180ms. still watching.
Sam (CS): notifying impacted customers with a note: "we're mitigating streaming stalls, expect improved latency in minutes; no data exposure."
Alex: checking runtime logs: a subset of pods still emit occasional stall traces referencing "epoll backlog" and slow writes to NGINX sidecar. Nginx sidecar restarts correlate with 502s earlier.
Anna (SRE): ok, possible root cause: sidecar backpressure + config change to write buffers caused cascading stalls. Plan: keep routing fallback + disabled batching, monitor autoscaler scale up, track sidecar restarts.
Maya: autoscaler added 2 nodes, new pods come up healthy. p99 now ~480ms.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: INCIDENT: mitigation successful, SLO back within target. please validate for 30m before incident close.
Kevin (Product): good job. please prepare a short incident summary for customers and ops postmortem. Include timeline, config change, mitigations, and next actions.
Anna (SRE): noted. immediate next actions: 1) revert sidecar buffer change permanently until we can load-test different values, 2) add alert that correlates sidecar restarts with p99 spikes, 3) run a full canary for async-write-buffer change in staging with streaming load.
Maya: I'll own the follow-ups, will open a postmortem and link the timeline.
Sam (CS): I'll follow up with customers and share the status note.
Alex: adding logs and flamegraphs to the incident thread.
Maya: thanks all. keeping thread open for 30m as required. :thumbsup:
